title: Nature's Treasures
seo_title: Nature's Treasures Class 6 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11)
standard_text: Natural resources: air, water, sunlight, soil, forests, minerals and fossil fuels; renewable and non-renewable resources; their uses; conserving resources with reduce, reuse and recycle (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 11: air, water, sunlight, soil, forests, minerals and fossil fuels, renewable and non-renewable resources and how to conserve them. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Nature gives us air, water, soil and energy.
key_sub: Renewable resources are replaced; non-renewable ones run out.
body_html:
How to think about it

Natural resources are useful things we get from nature: air (about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen), water, sunlight, wind, soil, forests and minerals. Sunlight, wind and water are renewable, but coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels that took millions of years to form and will run out.

We must use resources wisely: reduce, reuse and recycle, save water and electricity, plant trees and use solar and wind energy where we can.

Example

Is coal renewable?

it took millions of years to form

Answer: no: non-renewable

Example

Main gas in the air?

about 78%

Answer: nitrogen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking oxygen is the main gas in air.
  • Calling petroleum renewable.
  • Thinking resources never run out.

faq.q: Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
faq.a: They formed from the buried remains of plants and animals over millions of years.

faq.q: How can we conserve natural resources?
faq.a: By reducing use, reusing and recycling, saving water and electricity, planting trees and using renewable energy.
